name: Frame Rate
description: Convert between PAL and NTSC, or to any frame rate
longDescription:
Changes how many frames per second the output runs at.

Its first use is standards conversion — a tape that was converted from NTSC to PAL (or the reverse) at some point in its life, and now needs to play at the right speed on your equipment. Converting an already-converted tape repairs damage that is already in the source: leaving it alone means either judder or a 4% speed error.

Choose Custom to type any rate from 1 to 240 fps — 24 to 48 or 60 fps, for example. Raising the rate this way makes motion look smoother, but every added frame is generated, not photographed, so the file is no longer a faithful record of what was shot. Keep the original if that matters. Type NTSC rates as 23.976, 29.97 or 59.94 and they are converted exactly.

Motion interpolation gives the smoothest result and is usually invisible on a pan, but it can warp edges where something passes in front of something else. Repeat frames invents nothing at all and judders instead — the honest choice for an archival master.

AI interpolation (RIFE) builds the new frames with a neural network on your graphics card. On real footage it is somewhat more accurate than motion interpolation, but it is several times slower and needs a GPU with Vulkan support (any Apple Silicon Mac, or a Windows/Linux PC with a current graphics driver). If this computer can't run it, VapourBox says why as soon as you choose it.

This pass runs last, after everything else.

methods.name: Motion interpolation
methods.description: Builds the new frames from the motion between the real ones. Smoothest result; can warp edges where objects overlap.

methods.name: AI interpolation (RIFE)
methods.description: Builds the new frames with the RIFE 4.26 neural network on the GPU. Somewhat more accurate than motion interpolation, several times slower; needs Vulkan.

methods.name: Repeat frames
methods.description: Repeats or drops whole frames. Invents nothing, but motion judders.

ui.label: Method
ui.description: How the new frames are produced.

ui.label: Target rate
ui.description: The frame rate the output should run at. Custom lets you type any rate.

ui.label: Custom rate (fps)
ui.description: Any rate from 1 to 240, e.g. 48 or 60. NTSC rates (23.976, 29.97, 59.94) are converted exactly.

ui.label: Block size
ui.description: Motion is estimated in blocks of this size. Larger is faster and coarser.

ui.label: Block overlap
ui.description: How much neighbouring blocks overlap. More overlap hides block edges at some cost in speed.
